A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original polynomial-extrapolation and physical-motion prediction experiments in Section 5 and Appendix E, including numerical errors and prediction examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds Boolean-data experiments on low-degree bias, latent-variable identification, and out-of-distribution generalization in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The proposed mixed-activation MLP recipe and its application to transformer MLP blocks remain unchanged. Appendix C supplies experimental instantiations of the existing theoretical framework, without introducing a new proposed algorithm or objective.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds empirical coverage of a 10-bit latent-variable generator, parity-task representation learning, and prediction under Hamming-ball distribution shifts. These settings were theoretical rather than experimentally evaluated in v1. The polynomial and physical-motion tasks are retained.

E2.justification: New Figure 5 compares MLPs using oracle latent representations against MLPs without those representations, adding a comparison absent from v1. The existing ReLU-MLP and transformer comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new experiments introduce Hamming-ball versus full-cube sampling, task counts of 1, 4, 8, and 64, task-degree limits of 2, 3, and 4, linear-probe MSE evaluation, and oracle-representation controls. The reported protocols for the retained polynomial and physical-motion experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures 3–5 test whether restricted training support exposes low-degree bias, whether increasing task count improves latent identification, and whether oracle latents improve OOD prediction. These directly examine theoretical premises and predictions beyond v1's retained extrapolation and collision case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run averages for physical-motion results and violin plots over 50 sampled polynomials per degree. The new numerical experiments add no reported run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: New Figures 3–5 report persistent OOD error under restricted sampling, lower latent-identification error with 64 versus one task, and near-zero OOD error using oracle latents. Existing results are retained: Figure 2c still reports transformer/ours MSEs of 0.16/0.07 for parabolic motion and 0.29/0.13 for collision.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.9 substantially reformulates its degree assumptions: v1 uses deg(h composed with ψ)=q≥k, whereas v3 sets deg(h)=q>k and additionally requires deg(h composed with ψ)>k−q+r. Appendix E.7 correspondingly revises the orthogonality argument. Definition 3.6 also explicitly requires a nonempty feasible set.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims: multitask low-degree bias enables latent recovery, architecture compatibility matters, and the proposed architectural changes improve the illustrated tasks. The new experiments support these retained claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix B explains limitations of continuous Fourier, polynomial-order, and compression-based complexity measures. Appendix C connects reported activation sensitivity to basis compatibility and ReLU's imperfect low-degree bias. The principal limitations and future directions from v1 remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents the new generator explicitly in Table 1 and provides SGD, quadratic-activation, and MLP-depth information for the numerical studies. The reported GPU list changes from V100/A100/H100 to V100/A100; this disclosure change does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds Jiang et al. (2023) on compressor-based classification and expands positioning against alternative complexity measures. The main related-work discussion remains stable. Kang et al.'s change from a 2024 preprint to a 2025 conference reference concerns the same work.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose revisions, removes the duplicated linear-representation-hypothesis paragraph, adds acknowledgements and appendix sections, and updates cross-references. The main narrative and the ordering of retained substantive sections remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 1 and three multipanel experimental figures. Figure 2 expands from a small single-column display to full width, substantially improving readability. Existing appendix figures are redistributed and renumbered, with their original plotted content retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix C adds useful direct checks of low-degree bias and latent identification that v1's architectural demonstrations addressed only indirectly. The revised degree conditions in Theorem 4.9 and enlarged Figure 2 also improve precision and readability. The overall gain remains limited: the new evidence uses one small Boolean generator, the OOD comparison uses oracle latents, and run variability is unreported.
